simple.meaning: חֲטָאָה (chăṭâʼâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an offence , or a sacrifice for it.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Genesis, Exodus, 2 Kings, Psalms, beginning at Genesis 20:9. Its contexts include family line, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲטָאָה (H2401).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֲטָאָה (chăṭâʼâh) / H2401 is traced through Genesis 20:9, Exodus 32:21, Exodus 32:30, Exodus 32:31 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: an offence , or a sacrifice for it
definitions.full: H2401. chataah חֲטָאָה noun feminine sin, sin-offering (?) — 1 sin , chiefly in the phrase ׳ח גְדֹלָה great sin Gen 20:9 (E) Exod 32:21 , 30 , 31 (JE), 2Kin 17:21 ; ח ׳כְּסוּי Psa 32:1 he whose sin is covered is blessed; but the prayer of the wicked becomes sin when he is judged 109:7 . 2 sin-offering (according to most) וחטאה עולה Psa 40:7 whole burnt-offering and sin-offering (so Vrss Thes MV SS and others, but < whole burnt-offering with sin see Br MP 329 ).

occurrences.englishText: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
Moses said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you, that you have brought a great sin on them?”
On the next day, Moses said to the people, “You have sinned a great sin. Now I will go up to Yahweh. Perhaps I shall make atonement for your sin.”
Moses returned to Yahweh, and said, “Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made themselves gods of gold.
For he tore Israel from David’s house; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drove Israel from following Yahweh, and made them sin a great sin.
Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven,
Then I said, “Behold, I have come.
When he is judged, let him come out guilty.
